cause: Context Pack was frozen before development started.
impact: The line has an evidence-bound starting context.
lesson: Freeze the initial context before changing implementation state.

cause: The required RED probes ran before the shared opened-descriptor seam and still observed the path-backed artifact download and classification artifact/receipt reads.
impact: TDD RED observed 4 failed, 1 passed, 88 deselected, 1 warning; the missing shared module and legacy FileResponse were the expected pre-GREEN failures.
lesson: Run live repository, download, and consumer replacement probes before implementation and make every artifact byte read use one no-follow opened descriptor.

cause: The first RED command used a selector that matched no tests, so pytest exited with code 5 after reporting 93 deselected tests.
impact: No implementation state changed; the corrected selector was then executed and produced the intended RED evidence.
lesson: Validate focused selectors once before relying on their test counts, and record command-selection errors separately from product failures.

cause: The first GREEN focused run exposed a missing read_json import after the consumer path was migrated to the shared opened-file seam.
impact: The focused run stopped with two NameError failures before the final import correction; no persisted artifact or external worktree was affected.
lesson: After extracting a shared file seam, rerun focused consumers and restore only imports needed for the index authority without reintroducing path reads.

cause: A status subcommand was attempted even though devline_control.py exposes verify, retrospective, and related commands but no status command.
impact: The command exited with code 2 and did not mutate formal records; the supported verify and retrospective commands remain the closeout path.
lesson: Use the documented formal CLI surface and treat unsupported status checks as command errors rather than inventing a new control path.

cause: One temporary formal event object briefly contained a duplicate JSON key, so the append command rejected it before changing the event chain.
impact: The command exited with code 2 and did not mutate formal records; the duplicate key was removed and the same event was appended successfully.
lesson: Let the formal CLI reject duplicate-key event input and validate temporary JSON before append; never bypass the append-only control path.

cause: The shared repository/file-integrity seam now applies the bounded grammar, no-follow descriptor traversal, regular-file fstat, and same-open-descriptor hash/read to list validation, download, and classification artifact/receipt consumers.
impact: Final evidence: production 93 passed; TOCTOU/HTTP focus 6 passed; valid HTTP download and run-detail consumer passed; replacement callbacks executed at the live helper and external symlink replacement returned typed fail-closed errors with no wrapper, facts, receipt, or side effect.
lesson: Keep one server-owned opened-file seam below every artifact byte consumer and prove the replacement callback runs at the live helper before declaring TOCTOU GREEN.

cause: The existing classification production bindings and typed Agent, Notebook, and Report projections remain intact after the shared opened-file seam migration.
impact: The four focused classification contract suites passed 49 tests; split, fold, OOF, holdout, weights, calibration, threshold, identity, evidence, and typed consumer contracts remained green.
lesson: Keep repository/file integrity enforcement below the classification producer and typed consumer contracts, then rerun the complete classification contract focus.

cause: The existing tests/test_api.py artifacts focus retains two async completed-run fixture assumptions for report and report_html that are unrelated to the shared artifact-integrity boundary.
impact: Observed result: 2 failed, 6 passed, 31 deselected, 1 warning; report producer and root/other worktrees were not modified, so this remains a known gate.
lesson: Keep pre-existing report-fixture failures separate from repository and HTTP artifact-integrity evidence, and do not alter the report producer to manufacture a green gate.

cause: The existing v1.8.6 consumer route fixture supplies a non-canonical legacy prediction_result record, while the predecessor strict artifact-index validator rejects incomplete records before the route detail projection.
impact: Observed result: 1 failed, 3 passed; the failure is unchanged by this remediation and remains outside the frozen scope because it predates the shared seam and does not involve classification artifact/receipt reads.
lesson: Baseline legacy consumers separately from strict canonical artifact-index validation; do not relax the security validator or change unrelated projection fixtures in this line.

cause: The existing artifact-integrity fixture supplies incomplete non-canonical records, so the strict index validator returns ARTIFACTS_INDEX_INVALID before the older endpoint-level 200 and 409 assertions execute.
impact: Observed result: 3 failed, 1 warning; remediation-14 production/HTTP tests already cover canonical missing, non-regular, digest mismatch, duplicate, path, type, and index-status behavior, so this legacy fixture gate remains outside scope.
lesson: Keep canonical integrity fixtures aligned with the validator contract in a separately scoped cleanup; do not weaken fail-closed validation to satisfy stale records.

cause: The shared seam and three consumers pass the required static safety checks after migration.
impact: compileall exited 0 and git diff --check exited 0; static inspection found no unsafe path/hash flow in the artifact download or classification artifact/receipt readers, while unrelated report/export FileResponse endpoints remain unchanged.
lesson: Pair focused runtime probes with compileall and diff-check, then inspect remaining path APIs to distinguish unrelated endpoints from the hardened seam.

cause: The explicit artifact allowlist is a compatibility snapshot and may drift as producers evolve; widening it during this TOCTOU remediation would copy unsourced producer constants into a security validator.
impact: Bounded P2 follow-up: audit producer vocabulary or establish a server-owned registry in a separately scoped line; remediation-14 leaves the allowlist unchanged.
lesson: Treat artifact-type allowlist drift as a separately evidenced compatibility review rather than copying more constants into a security boundary.

cause: The remediation-14 implementation, focused evidence, known gates, bounded P2 follow-up, and formal records are complete for the package-local line.
impact: GREEN evidence: production 93 passed; TOCTOU/HTTP focus 6 passed; classification contracts 49 passed; compileall and diff-check passed. Known: API artifacts 2 failed/6 passed/31 deselected/1 warning, legacy consumer 1 failed/3 passed, artifact-integrity fixture 3 failed/1 warning. Browser, provider, central, host, full-gate, merge, tag, and release acceptance remain NOT VERIFIED.
lesson: Close a package-local remediation only with exact focused evidence, explicit inherited fixture gates, and a separate statement for every unperformed external acceptance boundary.
